newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Yilmaz maps out anti-Islamist strategy.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Yilmaz maps out anti-Islamist strategy.

text.p: Turkish prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz began a meeting of his conservative Motherland Party on Monday to map out strategy for his bid to forge an anti-Islamist coalition.
"We will debate which parties we will contact and how we will go about it," Motherland deputy chairman Ahad Andican told Reuters.
The Turkish press said Yilmaz and his aides would discuss ways to woo fellow conservatives from Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller's True Path Party into the planned secularist alliance.
Istanbul shares leaped 5.3 percent in morning trading on hopes that free-marketeer Yilmaz would overcome the obstacles in the way of forming a coalition, brokers said.
A dissident MP from Ciller's faction who resigned on Sunday denied reports he would join Motherland but said he would back Yilmaz at a vote of confidence, Anatolian news agency said.
"I will vote for him," the agency quoted MP Haluk Muftuler as saying. He predicted that two or three other MPs were ready to quit True Path in an anti-Islamist protest.
Yilmaz is around a dozen votes short of the simple majority he would need to win a confidence vote. He is opposed by a pro-Islamic alliance that has 282 votes in the 550-seat chamber.
President Suleyman Demirel last week nominated Yilmaz to put together a government after the resignation of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, who stays on as caretaker for the time being.
Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, stepped down after months of open criticism from the secularist army.
Yilmaz, a former prime minister, is to meet the leaders of four political parties on Tuesday for talks on setting up a new government.
No meeting with Erbakan, head of the Islam-based Welfare Party, is on his schedule, party officials said.
